top_choice_rationale: The diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos is a clue from nature that no theory predicted at that level, seen in several independent analysis channels with different backgrounds, and the citation (diffuse flux only, leaving TXS 0506+056, NGC 1068 and the Galactic plane out) stays inside what is established. The Halzen-Karle attribution is the open weakness and I would follow the historical record if it points to a different second name, but the discovery itself is mature. The optical lattice clock (P002) is a superb but mainly capability-and-accuracy result with the redefinition of the second still prospective; topological insulators (P001) have the strongest concept but the three-name cap forces an exclusion (Hasan, BHZ with Zhang deceased) and sits near the 2016 prize. Any award is preferred to no award.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; no tie to Halzen, Karle, Katori, Ye, Kane, Mele or Molenkamp (Gross, Van Riet and the Uppsala string group are unrelated; Eriksson is a department colleague in a different field)
